 Judgment
MFA No.103340/2019 is filed by the appellants- claimants for seeking enhancement of compensation.

2. MFA No.100983/2019 is filed by the Insurance Company challenging the liability on the ground that the driver of the lorry was not holding driving license since as on the date of accident it was expired.
3. The factum of the accident is not in dispute.
4. The offending vehicle is lorry bearing No. KA-31/B-0777 which has caused accident resulting to the death of the deceased.
5. LIABILITY:
The learned counsel for the Insurance Company submitted that the accident was caused on 20.06.2016 and the driving license of the driver of the lorry was expired on 25.02.2016.
But, the application for renewal of license was filed on 01.03.2017 i.e. after one year one month.
Hence, as on the date of accident, there NC: 2023:KHC-D:9116 was no valid driving license.

Hence,
Insurance Company is not liable to pay the compensation by indemnifying the owner.

6. On the other hand, learned counsel for the claimant submitted that the driving license to drive heavy goods vehicle is renewed with effect from 22.06.2016 and in this regard, the evidence given by the RW.2-RTO Officer stating that the application filed for renewal is on 01.03.2017 is not correct.
Therefore, submitted that as per Ex.P8 and Ex.R3 driving license extracts, it is proved that from 26.02.2016, the driving license to drive the transport vehicle is renewed.
Therefore, submitted that as on the date of accident, driver was holding driving license.
7. EX.P8 is the driving license extract produced by the claimants which shows that the driving license to drive heavy goods vehicle (Transport) is renewed from 26.02.2016 to 26.02.2019.

Ex.R3 is the driving license extract produced by the Insurance Company, in which also, it is stated that the driving license for driving the NC: 2023:KHC-D:9116 transport vehicle is renewed with effect from 26.02.2016.

But, the RW.2-RTO officer had stated that both the Ex.P8 and Ex.R3 are issued from the RTO office only but stated that application for renewal is filed on 01.03.2017 that is after one year one month from the date of expiry of driving license.
The RW.2-RTO officer has not stated on what basis the application for renewal is filed on 01.03.2017.
But, in the oral evidence stated that application is filed on 01.03.2017.
But in the documentary evidences driving license extracts Ex.P8 and Ex.R3 which are issued from the office of RTO only as per his evidence.
Therefore, the contents in Ex.R3 that the driving license for transport vehicle is renewed from 26.02.2016.

When both these documentary evidence prove that the driving license was renewed with effect from 26.02.2016, but V.Lakshmi W/O Late Raju vs Hanumanthappa S/O Pulakurthi ... on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67017549/
4
the oral evidence stating that the application for renewal is filed on 01.03.2017 cannot be considered because the said evidence is without any basis or any record.

If RW.2-RTO officer substantiated his evidence that the application is filed on 01.03.2017 with office records/files then, his NC:
2023:KHC-D:9116 evidence would have been considered in believing the application is filed on 01.03.2017 but without any records, he had stated that the application is filed on 01.03.2017 is not believable.
But, at the same time, he had admitted that both exhibits P8 and R3 are issued from his office and these documents show that driving license was renewed from 26.02.2016.
Therefore, it is proved that the driver of lorry has got renewed driving license and was having a valid driving license of heavy goods vehicle(transport).
In this regard the submission urged by the Insurance Company is liable to be rejected.

Regarding quantum of compensation:
8.
The deceased was aged 24 years, therefore, the appropriate multiplier applicable is "18".
The claimants are wife, father and major brother.
The Tribunal has committed error in deducting 1/4th amount towards personal and living expenses, but 1/3rd ought to have been deducted.

The accident was caused on 26.02.2016, therefore, the notional income of Rs.8,750/- is to be taken NC: 2023:KHC-D:9116 into consideration as per the Notional Income Chart recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.
The deceased was a mason by profession.
Therefore, 40% of income is to be added towards loss of future prospects in life.

Therefore,
compensation under the head loss of dependency is re-assessed and quantified as follows:
Rs.8,750/-+Rs.3,500/- (40% of Rs.8,750/-) = Rs.12,250/- Rs.12,250/- x 2/3 x 18 x 12=Rs.17,64,000/-
Accordingly, compensation of Rs.17,64,000/- is awarded under the head loss of dependency.

9. The Tribunal has committed error in awarding compensation under other heads,
which ought to be modified.
10.
There are three claimants.

Therefore, the claimants are entitled to Rs.16,500/-
(Rs.15,000/- + 10% escalation) under the head loss of estate and NC:
2023:KHC-D:9116 Rs.16,500/- under the head transportation of dead body and funeral expenses.
11.
The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.50,000/- towards loss of consortium to petitioner No.1 and Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of love and affection.
The loss of love and affection and loss of consortium are having the same connotation.
As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Limited v. Nanu Ram & Others1, each claimants are entitled for Rs.40,000/-.

Therefore, compensation of Rs.1,32,000/- (Rs.40,000/- x 3 dependants + 10%
escalation)
is awarded under the head loss of consortium including loss of love and affection.

12. Thus, in all the appellants/claimants are entitled to total compensation determined by this Court as follows:
2018 ACJ 2782 - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:9116 1 Loss of dependency Rs. 17,64,000/- 2 Loss of estate Rs.
16,500/-
3 Transportation of dead Rs.
 body and funeral 16,500/-
 expenses  4 Loss of consortium Rs. 1,32,000/-
 Total Rs. 19,29,000/-
13.
The Tribunal has granted interest at the rate of 9% p.a., and the same is scaled down to 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
14. The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.14,45,000/-, but the appellants/claimants are entitled to total compensation of Rs.19,29,000/-.

Hence,
the appellants/claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.4,84,000/-
(Rs.19,29,000/- -
Rs.14,45,000/-).
Therefore, the appellants/claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.4,84,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i. MFA.No.103340/2019 filed by the claimants is allowed-in-part.
ii. MFA.No.100983/2019 filed by the Insurance Company is allowed-in-part.

iv. No order as to costs.
v. The appellants/claimants are not entitled for interest for the delay period of 279 days in filing the appeal.
